facts.fact_text: On 29 April 2008 the applicants jointly notified the Beyoğlu district governor that they would be gathering before the Taksim Atatürk memorial on 1 May 2008 at 1 p.m.
The applicants notified the Beyoğlu district governor that the purpose of the gathering was to celebrate Labour Day.
The applicants notified the Beyoğlu district governor that the purpose of the gathering was to commemorate their friends who had lost their lives during the demonstrations of 1 May 1977.

At approximately 6 a.m. on 1 May 2008, members of the Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Turkey (DİSK) and the Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions (KESK) began gathering in front of the DİSK headquarters located in the district of Şişli for Labour Day celebrations.

The members of the group refused to disperse, arguing that they were merely waiting in front of the DİSK headquarters, which was a pedestrian area, and that they were not violating the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) in any way.
At approximately 10.30 a.m. on 1 May 2008, the group of demonstrators broke up of its own accord to forestall any further violence.
No prosecution was initiated against the applicants in relation to the events of 1 May 2008.
Article 34 of the Turkish Constitution provides that everyone has the right to hold unarmed and peaceful meetings and demonstration marches without prior permission.
On 30 April 2008 the Beyoğlu district governor authorised a gathering at the Taksim Atatürk memorial for representatives of trade unions only.
The Beyoğlu district governor specifically indicated that a demonstration on a larger scale at the Taksim Atatürk memorial was not authorised.
The authorities held that any demonstration held in Taksim Square on 1 May 2008 would be unlawful and unconstitutional on account of possible provocations and disruption of traffic and public order.
At around 6.30 a.m. on 1 May 2008, the police asked the group gathered in front of the DİSK headquarters in Şişli to disperse.
The police warned the group gathered in front of the DİSK headquarters in Şişli that they were acting in violation of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
The police proceeded to disperse the group gathered in front of the DİSK headquarters in Şişli by spraying them with pressurised water, paint and tear gas, both inside and outside the DİSK building.
Similar police interventions occurred over the next couple of hours after 6.30 a.m. on 1 May 2008 with increasing intensity.
Some of the demonstrators were injured as a result of the use of force by the police on 1 May 2008 in the district of Şişli.
While injured demonstrators were trying to reach the nearby Şişli Etfal Hospital for medical care, they were chased by the police.
While injured demonstrators were trying to reach Şişli Etfal Hospital for medical care, they were subjected to gas attacks even within the hospital premises.
Some members of the DİSK were arrested on 1 May 2008.

Section 22 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibits demonstrations and processions on public streets, in parks, places of worship and buildings in which public services are based.

Section 22 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that demonstrations organised in public squares have to comply with security instructions and not disrupt individuals' movements or public transport.

Section 24 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that demonstrations and processions which do not comply with the provisions of that law will be dispersed by force on the order of the governor's office and after the demonstrators are warned.

The Minister of the Interior issued a press statement declaring that the authorities were in possession of intelligence reports which precluded them from authorising any demonstration in Taksim Square, for security reasons.

The Government's spokesman issued a press statement declaring that the authorities were in possession of intelligence reports which precluded them from authorising any demonstration in Taksim Square, for security reasons.

The Istanbul Governor's office issued a press statement declaring that the authorities were in possession of intelligence reports which precluded them from authorising any demonstration in Taksim Square, for security reasons.
The authorities held that any demonstration held in Taksim Square on 1 May 2008 would be unlawful and unconstitutional on account of possible provocations and disruption of traffic and public order.
The authorities stated that they were going to shut down certain schools in the nearby districts of Taksim Square on 1 May 2008 as a security measure.
The authorities stated that they were going to stop the operation of ferries and subways on 1 May 2008 as a security measure.
The authorities stated that they were going to block the roads leading to Taksim Square on 1 May 2008 as a security measure.
The authorities stated that they were going to deploy extra police on 1 May 2008 as a security measure.
As alternative locations for the demonstration, the Istanbul Governor's office indicated four other squares: two on the European side and two on the Anatolian side of Istanbul.
